pr_title: Wrap angles to (-pi, pi) in momentum calculation.
pr_body:
Fixes bug #41527 (Excess angular momentum when 2D kinematic body rotates beyond 180 degrees) by limiting the difference in angle between frames to the range (-pi, pi). 

This was the most minimal solution I could think of; it uses the standard library remainder function to produce the difference between the angle and the nearest integer multiple of 2pi. Another solution might be to add a method to the Transform2D class that gets an orientation vector, then use an angle-between-vectors method - this would avoid computing two angles then taking a modulus.

This change was actually tested on 3.2.2-stable; I assume the same change will work in 4.0, however I cannot get it to compile on my machine.

_Bugsquad edit:_ Fixes #31940, fixes #41527.
pr_comments:
I see that it does not build on Windows (I assumed M_PI would be available there, too). Let me refactor into a platform-agnostic unwrap function.

Edit: no refactor needed, I see you've already defined Math_PI elsewhere.

Is there any reason this can't be merged into a 3.2/3.3 release?
Edit: sorry was looking at the milestone bar. Looked right over the cherry pick 3.2 label.
No, and that's why it has the `cherrypick:3.2` label which means that it's queued for merging into `3.2`.

issue_context.title: Excess angular momentum when 2D kinematic body rotates beyond 180 degrees
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.2-stable, also latest master as of this writing (git commit 443686d724ce8ac58dcdf09389e9f996aee866c1).


**OS/device including version:**
All (tested on Ubuntu 20.04, Windows 10).


**Issue description:**
When a KinematicBody2D rotates beyond 180 degrees, any RigidBody in contact with it flies away.

This is because the 2D physics server calculates angular momentum using the difference between the previous update's angle and the current angle. When rotating beyond 180, the angle wraps around to -180, and the server calculates a difference of nearly 360 degrees between frame, resulting in a very high angular momentum. This is then propagated to colliding physics bodies.

See reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/godot/comments/ifxtf5/is_this_something_that_should_be_fixed_for/

**Steps to reproduce:**
Have a KinematicBody2D rotating to nearly 180 degrees. Place a RigidBody on top. As soon as the KinematicBody2D passes 180 degrees of rotation, the RigidBody will fly away with large amounts of momentum.

**Minimal reproduction project:**
See https://github.com/Tobzster/KinematicBody2D_Angular_Velocity_Glitch from the author of the reddit thread.

review_comments: Why `2.0 * Math_PI` to wrap to `(-pi, pi)`? Also, prefer `Math_TAU` to `2.0 * Math_PI`.

The remainder function takes the (signed) distance between the first parameter and the nearest integer multiple of the second value. By way of analogy, remainder is to rounding as the modulus is to truncation.

It may help to mentally step through all of the ranges for the angle. Between 0 and pi, the nearest integer multiple of 2\*pi is 0, so the angle is unchanged. Between pi and 2\*pi, the nearest integer multiple is 2pi, and the distance is `angle - 2*pi` (negative, because the angle is less than the nearest multiple), so the angle gets transformed to the range (-pi, 0), which is correct. Similarly, between -pi to 0, the nearest multiple is 0 and the angle is unchanged. Between -2pi and -pi, the nearest angle is -2pi and the distance is `angle - (-2pi)`.

I agree that the remainder function is confusingly-named. However, I think we don't need to make a habit of describing functions from the standard library wherever they are used.

Perhaps it would be better to define an inline wrap_angle function to make it clearer the intent of this line, and that way the implementation could also be changed with something more performant later if someone decided to do that. 

I also prefer 2.0*Math_PI in this case, because it makes the relationship to the range (-pi, pi) more explicit. 

That said as of right now this is the only place I'm aware of where angle wrapping is needed, so I'd lean against adding complexity and optimization prematurely. This is a bugfix PR, another PR could be used to redesign (and if I were doing that, I'd change to a stable angle-between-vectors algorithm instead of subtracting angles).
We do have `fposmod`, which works for angles, but gives outputs on the range (0, TAU) if used with TAU or 2PI, so we would have to add a check with `> Math_PI` and then do `-= Math_TAU`.
So is this good to merge as is, or should this be further documented/changed?
I think it's good to merge as it is.
